'''Marco Stefano Belinelli''' ({{IPA|it|ˈmarko beliˈnɛlli}}; born 25 March 1986) is an Italian former professional [[basketball]] player. He was selected 18th overall in the [[2007 NBA draft]] by the [[Golden State Warriors]]. In 2014, he won the NBA championship with the [[San Antonio Spurs]], becoming the first Italian player to do so. He won the [[Three-Point Contest]] during the [[2014 NBA All-Star Game|2014 NBA All-Star Weekend]]. He played in the [[EuroBasket 2007|2007]], [[EuroBasket 2011|2011]], [[EuroBasket 2013|2013]], [[EuroBasket 2015|2015]], and [[EuroBasket 2017|2017]] editions of the [[FIBA EuroBasket]] and the [[2006 FIBA World Championship|2006]] and [[2019 FIBA World Championship|2019]] editions of the [[FIBA World Championship]] with the [[Italy national basketball team|Italian national basketball team]].

==Professional career==
===Virtus and Fortitudo Bologna (2002–2007)===
Belinelli played in the Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A|Serie A]] and the [[EuroLeague]] for [[Virtus Bologna]] and [[Fortitudo Pallacanestro Bologna|Fortitudo Bologna]]. In 2004, he lost the [[2004 EuroLeague Final Four|EuroLeague Finals]] against [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]], and in 2005, he won the Serie A title with Fortitudo.

===NBA (2007–2020)===
====Golden State Warriors (2007–2009)====
After being selected #18 in the first round of the [[2007 NBA draft]] by the [[Golden State Warriors]], Belinelli scored 37 points in his first [[NBA Summer League]] game against the [[New Orleans Hornets]], going 14-on-20 from the field, including 5-on-7 from [[three-point field goal|behind the arc]],<ref>[http://www.nba.com/summerleague2007/games/boxscore.jsp?gameId=1520700005 NBA.com : Summer League 2007<!-- Bot generated title -->] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070712095113/http://www.nba.com/summerleague2007/games/boxscore.jsp?gameId=1520700005 |date=2007-07-12 }}</ref> adding 5 boards, 2 assists and 1 steal to help the Warriors earn a 110–102 win. His performance is tied for second for the highest scoring game ever in Vegas summer league history, behind [[Keith Bogans]]' 38 scored as a member of the [[Orlando Magic]] in 2004. Belinelli finished his Summer League scoring an average of 22.8 points per game in 4 games with the Warriors, before returning to [[Italy]] to be part of the Italian national team for [[EuroBasket 2007]]. On 19 December 2008, he scored 27 points, in a game the Warriors lost to [[Atlanta Hawks]].

====Toronto Raptors (2009–2010)====
On 30 July 2009, he was traded to the [[Toronto Raptors]] for [[Devean George]],<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/belinelli_trade073009.html | title=Raptors Acquire Belinelli From Golden State | work=[[NBA.com]] | date=2009-07-30 | access-date=2009-07-30}}</ref> joining [[Italy national basketball team|Italian national squad]] teammate [[Andrea Bargnani]]. He played his first NBA game as a starter for Toronto on 2 February 2010 against the Indiana Pacers.{{citation needed|date=January 2025}}

====New Orleans Hornets (2010–2012)====
On 11 August 2010, he was traded to the [[New Orleans Hornets]] for [[Julian Wright]].<ref>{{cite web| url=http://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets_acquire_belinelli_2010_08_11.html | title=HORNETS ACQUIRE BELINELLI | work=[[NBA.com]] | date=2010-08-11 | access-date=2010-08-11}}</ref> After the 2010–11 season, he became a restricted free agent. On 13 December 2011, he signed the $3.4 million qualifying offer to stay with the Hornets for one more year.<ref>{{cite web| url=http://www.nba.com/hornets/news/marco_belinelli_signs_qualifyi_2011_12_13.html | title=MARCO BELINELLI SIGNS QUALIFYING OFFER | work=[[NBA.com]] | date=2011-12-13 | access-date=2011-12-14}}</ref>

====Chicago Bulls (2012–2013)====
On 24 July 2012, Belinelli signed a one-year, $1.96 million contract with the [[Chicago Bulls]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/2012/news/07/24/bulls-move.ap/index.html|title=Bulls sign guard Belinelli, formerly of Hornets|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=24 July 2012|access-date=24 July 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120726162507/http://www.nba.com/2012/news/07/24/bulls-move.ap/index.html|archive-date=26 July 2012}}</ref> With the Bulls, Belinelli developed a reputation as a clutch player, hitting shots that include a game winning shot against the Celtics in overtime while falling down, a go-ahead layup against the [[Detroit Pistons]] after [[Joakim Noah]] saved the ball from going out of bounds, a game-winning lay-up with 20 seconds remaining against the [[Brooklyn Nets]], and a 3 pointer to give the Bulls a 1-point lead with 5 seconds remaining in a game vs. the [[Utah Jazz]].{{citation needed|date=January 2025}} Belinelli and [[Joakim Noah]] each scored 24 points in a Game 7 victory over the [[Brooklyn Nets]] in the first round of the [[2013 NBA Playoffs]].<ref>[https://www.nba.com/games/20130504/CHIBKN/gameinfo.html#nbaGIboxscore Bulls at Nets, 4 May 2013]</ref>

====San Antonio Spurs (2013–2015)====
On 11 July 2013, Belinelli signed a two-year, $5.6 million contract with the [[San Antonio Spurs]].<ref>[https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/130711_spurs_sign_marco_belinelli Spurs Sign Marco Belinelli]</ref>

On 2 January 2014, Belinelli scored a career-high 32 points in a 105–101 loss to the [[New York Knicks]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 3, 2014 |title=Carmelo Anthony, Knicks stun Spurs in San Antonio |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400489350 |access-date=2024-11-05 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press |language=en}}</ref>

Belinelli also won the [[Three-Point Contest]] at the 2014 [[NBA All-Star Weekend]] in [[New Orleans]], beating [[Bradley Beal]] of the [[Washington Wizards]] at the second attempt in the final after Beal equaled Belinelli's score in the initial final round. In the tiebreaker, Belinelli made six straight shots at a single point, sweeping his fourth rack.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2014-02-15|title=Belinelli bests Beal to claim NBA 3-point title|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/allstar2014/story/_/id/10462244/2014-nba-all-star-game-marco-belinelli-wins-3-point-contest|access-date=2020-11-16|website=ESPN.com|language=en}}</ref>

In his first season with the Spurs, Belinelli posted career-highs on field goal percentage, three-point percentage, and free-throw percentage.

In Game 3 of the [[2014 NBA Finals]] against the two-time defending champion Miami Heat, Belinelli hit a crucial 3 pointer in the third quarter that increased San Antonio's lead back to double digits.{{citation needed|date=January 2025}} The Heat had rallied, cutting the Spurs' half-time lead of 21 points to just seven, before Belinelli's three-pointer. Upon winning the 2014 Finals, he became the first Italian player to win an NBA championship.{{citation needed|date=January 2025}}

====Kings, Hornets, Hawks and 76ers (2015–2018)====
On 13 July 2015, Belinelli signed a three-year, $19 million contract with the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/07132015-press-release|title=Kings Sign Rondo, Belinelli, Koufos|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=13 July 2015|access-date=13 July 2015}}</ref> On 30 December 2015, he scored a season-high 28 points in a loss to the Philadelphia 76ers.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151230/PHISAC/gameinfo.html|title=Sixers surprise Kings for 2nd win in 3 games|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=30 December 2015|access-date=31 December 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161202131916/http://www.nba.com/games/20151230/PHISAC/gameinfo.html|archive-date=2 December 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On 7 July 2016, Belinelli was traded to the [[Charlotte Hornets]] in exchange for the draft rights to [[Malachi Richardson]].<ref>[https://www.nba.com/hornets/press-releases/hornets-acquire-marco-belinelli-sacramento Hornets Acquire Marco Belinelli from Sacramento]</ref> On 20 June 2017, Belinelli was traded, along with [[Miles Plumlee]] and the 41st pick which became [[Tyler Dorsey]] in the [[2017 NBA draft]], to the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in exchange for [[Dwight Howard]] and the 31st overall pick ([[Frank Jackson (basketball)|Frank Jackson]]) in the 2017 NBA draft.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/hornets-acquire-howard-and-draft-pick-hawks|title=Hornets Acquire Howard and Draft Pick from Hawks|work=NBA.com|date=20 June 2017|access-date=20 June 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-acquire-plumlee-belinelli-dwight-howard-trade|title=Hawks Acquire Plumlee, Belinelli In Dwight Howard Trade|work=NBA.com|date=21 June 2017|access-date=21 June 2017}}</ref> On 9 February 2018, he was waived by the Hawks.<ref>{{cite web|title=Hawks Waive Marco Belinelli|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-waive-marco-belinelli|work=NBA.com|date=9 February 2018|access-date=9 February 2018}}</ref>

[[File:Marco Belinelli 18 (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright|Belinelli playing for the 76ers in 2018]]

On 12 February 2018, Belinelli signed with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] for the remainder of the season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Philadelphia 76ers Sign Marco Belinelli|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/philadelphia-76ers-sign-marco-belinelli|work=NBA.com|date=12 February 2018|access-date=12 February 2018}}</ref> In Game 3 of the Eastern Conference Semi-Finals against the [[Boston Celtics]], Marco made a two-point corner shot to send the game to overtime, 89–89. However, the 76ers would lose to the Celtics, 101–98.<ref>{{cite magazine|title=Watch: 76ers' Marco Belinelli Nails Buzzer Beater to Take Game 3 to Overtime Before Loss|url=https://www.si.com/nba/2018/05/05/celtics-sixers-game-3-nba-playoffs#:~:text=overtime%20on%20Saturday.-,The%2076ers'%20Marco%20Belinelli%20hit%20a%20buzzer%20beater%20to%20send,be%20called%20a%20two%2Dpointer| magazine=Sports Illustrated|date=5 May 2018}}</ref>

====Second stint with the Spurs (2018–2020)====
On 20 July 2018, Belinelli signed a two-year, $12 million contract with the [[San Antonio Spurs]], returning to the franchise for a second stint.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/spurs-sign-marco-belinelli|title=SPURS SIGN MARCO BELINELLI|work=NBA.com|date=20 July 2018|access-date=20 July 2018}}</ref>

===Virtus Bologna (2020–2025)===
[[File:Virtus Bologna EuroCup 2022.jpg|thumb|right|220px|Belinelli and teammates celebrating the [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]] victory in 2022]]
On 26 November 2020, Belinelli left the NBA and returned to Italy signing a three-year deal, until June 2023 with [[Virtus Bologna]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Marco Belinelli e' un nuovo giocatore di Virtus Segafredo Bologna |url=https://www.virtus.it/news/marco-belinelli-e-un-nuovo-giocatore-di-virtus-segafredo-bologna/ |website=virtus.it |access-date=26 November 2020 |language=it-IT |date=26 November 2020 |archive-date=4 December 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201204172653/https://www.virtus.it/news/marco-belinelli-e-un-nuovo-giocatore-di-virtus-segafredo-bologna/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> In April 2021, despite a winning record of 19–2, Virtus was defeated in the EuroCup's semifinals by [[BC UNICS|UNICS Kazan]].<ref>[https://bologna.repubblica.it/sport/2021/04/14/news/virtus-kazan-296460587/ Virtus, la notte più nera. In Eurolega vanno i russi], ''la Repubblica''</ref> However, the season ended with a great success. In fact, after having knocked out 3–0 both [[Universo Treviso Basket|Basket Treviso]] in the quarterfinals and [[New Basket Brindisi]] in the semifinals, on 11 June Virtus [[2021 LBA Playoffs|defeated 4–0]] its historic rival [[Olimpia Milano]] in the national finals, winning its 16th national title and the first one after twenty years.<ref>[https://www.gazzetta.it/Basket/SerieA/11-06-2021/basket-finale-scudetto-bologna-virtus-milano-olimpia-gara-4-4101900719362.shtml Virtus, sei magnifica! Bologna, scudetto dopo 20 anni, Milano schiacciata 4-0], ''Gazzetta dello Sport''</ref>

On 21 September 2021, the team won its second [[2021 Italian Basketball Supercup|Supercup]], defeating [[Olimpia Milano]] 90–84.<ref>[https://www.repubblica.it/sport/basket/2021/09/21/news/basket_supercoppa_alla_virtus_bologna_il_primo_trofeo_stagionale_milano_ancora_ko-318837432/ Basket, la Virtus Bologna vince la Supercoppa: Milano ancora ko], ''la Repubblica''</ref> Moreover, after having ousted [[BC Lietkabelis|Lietkabelis]], [[Ratiopharm Ulm|Ulm]] and [[Valencia Basket|Valencia]] in the first three rounds of the [[2022 EuroCup Basketball Playoffs|playoffs]], on 11 May 2022, Virtus defeated [[Bursaspor Basketbol|Frutti Extra Bursaspor]] by 80–67 at the Segafredo Arena, winning its first [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]] and qualifying for the [[EuroLeague]] after 14 years.<ref>{{cite web |title=Game Night: Virtus is the 7DAYS EuroCup champion and headed back to the EuroLeague! |url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/eurocup/news/game-night-a-new-7days-eurocup-champ-is-crowned-tonight/?pageTitle=Homepage&historyUrl=/eurocup/|website=euroleaguebasketball.net |date=11 May 2022}}</ref> However, despite having ended the regular season at the first place and having ousted 3–0 both [[U.S. Victoria Libertas Pallacanestro|Pesaro]] and [[Derthona Basket|Tortona]] in the first two rounds of playoffs, Virtus was defeated 4–2 in the national finals by Olimpia Milan.<ref>{{cite web |title=Olimpia Milano campione d'Italia, Virtus Bologna ko 81-64 in gara-6|url=https://sport.sky.it/basket/serie-a/2022/06/18/olimpia-milano-virtus-bologna-risultato|website=Sky Sport|date=18 June 2022}}</ref>

On 29 September 2022, after having ousted Milano in the semifinals, Virtus won its [[2022 Italian Basketball Supercup|third Supercup]], defeating 72–69 [[Dinamo Sassari|Banco di Sardegna Sassari]] and achieving a back-to-back, following the 2021 trophy.<ref>{{cite web |title=Supercoppa, trionfa la Virtus Bologna! Canestro decisivo di Mickey, Sassari cede 72-69|url=https://www.gazzetta.it/Basket/SerieA/29-09-2022/basket-supercoppa-trionfa-virtus-bologna-sassari-ko-72-69-450409276762.shtml|website=Gazzetta dello Sport|date=29 September 2022}}</ref> However, despite good premises Virtus ended the [[2022–23 EuroLeague|EuroLeague season]] at the 14th place, thus it did not qualify for the playoffs.<ref>[https://bolognabasket.org/virtus-il-punto-a-fine-eurolega/ Virtus, il punto a fine EuroLega]. BolognaBasket</ref> Moreover, the team was defeated in the [[Italian Basketball Cup]] final by [[Pallacanestro Brescia|Brescia]]. In June, after having ousted 3–0 both Brindisi and Tortona, Virtus was defeated 4–3 by Olimpia Milan in the national finals, following a series which was widely regarded among the best in the latest years of Italian basketball.<ref>[https://video.repubblica.it/sport/basket-milano-batte-bologna-nella-decisiva-gara-7-e-vince-il-suo-30esimo-scudetto-gli-highlights/447915/448883 Basket, Milano batte Bologna nella decisiva gara 7 e vince il suo 30esimo scudetto. Gli highlights]. la Repubblica</ref><ref>[https://www.rainews.it/articoli/2023/06/basket-serie-a-playoff-olimpia-milano-batte-virtus-bologna-in-gara-7-e-vince-lo-scudetto-al-forum-assago-c279332e-c2fa-46be-a199-3ff966b78a99.html Basket, Milano batte Bologna 67-55 nella finalissima e si conferma campione per la trentesima volta]. Rai News</ref>

On 7 July 2023, Belinelli renewed his contract with Virtus through 2025. On 24 September, after having ousted Olimpia Milano in the semifinals, Virtus won its [[2023 Italian Basketball Supercup|fourth Supercup]], and the third in a row, defeating 97–60 [[Pallacanestro Brescia|Germani Brescia]].<ref>[https://bologna.repubblica.it/sport/2023/09/24/news/una_virtus_esagerata_stravince_la_supercoppa-415671857/ Una Virtus esagerata stravince la Supercoppa]. la Repubblica</ref> Despite an impressive first half of the season, Virtus ended the EuroLeague regular season at the 10th place, qualifying only for the [[2023–24 EuroLeague#Play-in|play-in]], where after having defeated 67–64 [[Anadolu Efes]], it lost against [[Saski Baskonia|Baskonia]] 89–77, not qualifying for the playoffs.<ref>[https://www.rainews.it/tgr/emiliaromagna/articoli/2024/04/la-virtus-perde-lo-spareggio-con-il-baskonia-ed-e-decima-908bfb4e-0b89-4ece-879a-08b52af05723.html Basket, la Virtus perde lo spareggio con il Baskonia ed è decima]. Rai News</ref> Moreover, the Black V placed first during the Italian regular season but, after having knocked out [[Derthona Basket|Tortona]] by 3–2 and [[Reyer Venezia]] by 3–1, it lost the third consecutive final against Milan by 3–1.<ref>[https://www.eurosport.it/basket/serie-a/2023-2024/lolimpia-milano-chiude-sul-3-1-le-finali-con-la-virtus-bologna-e-il-terzo-scudetto-consecutivo-il-31o-della-storia_sto20010851/story.shtml L'Olimpia Milano chiude sul 3-1 le finali con la Virtus Bologna, è il terzo scudetto consevutivo e il 31° della storia]. EuroSport</ref>

In the following season Virtus ended the EuroLeague at the 17th place, after a disappointing regular season. After arriving first in the national championship season, Virtus eliminated Venezia 3–2 and their arch-rival Milan 3–1, reaching their fifth finals in a row. They then defeated Brescia 3–0, claiming the Italian championship title for the 17th time.<ref>[https://sport.sky.it/basket/serie-a/2025/06/17/brescia-virtus-bologna-gara-3-risultato La Virtus Bologna vince il suo 17° scudetto: 3-0 a Brescia in finale playoff]. Sky Sport</ref><ref>[https://www.ilpost.it/2025/06/17/virtus-bologna-scudetto-serie-a-basket-2025/ La Virtus Bologna ha vinto la Serie A di basket]. Il Post</ref> For Belinelli, this was the third ''scudetto'' of his career.

On 18 August 2025, Belinelli announced his retirement from professional basketball, concluding his 20-year professional career, citing that he gave the game of basketball "...my heart. Every piece of me. Every single day. Basketball gave me everything… and I gave it everything I had.” <ref>{{Cite web |last=TalkBasket.net |date=2025-08-18 |title=Marco Belinelli announces retirement |url=https://www.talkbasket.net/201632-marco-belinelli-announces-retirement |access-date=2025-08-18 |website=TalkBasket.net}}</ref>

==National team career==
[[File:Marco Belinelli.jpg|thumb|right|180px|Marco Belinelli with Italy's national team]]
Belinelli made his debut with the [[Italy national basketball team|Italian national team]] in the [[2006 FIBA World Championship]]. In that tournament, he scored 25 points against the [[United States men's national basketball team|United States national team]], including a dunk on [[Carmelo Anthony]]. In that tournament, he averaged 13.5 points per game, being the best scorer of his team.

He averaged 15.5 points per game at the [[2007 EuroBasket]], 12.0 points per game at the [[2011 EuroBasket]], 13.6 points per game at the [[2013 EuroBasket]], 16.3 points per game at the [[2015 EuroBasket]] and 17.9 points per game at the [[2017 EuroBasket]].
